gap: The claim that a temporal re-ranking wrapper is retrieval-agnostic is asserted but untested: TempRALM states it could extend any numeric-similarity retriever yet instantiates only the Atlas/Contriever dense retriever, and no retrieved work evaluates the same temporal wrapper across sparse and dense retrievers under matched budgets.

evidence.quote: our approach could be used to extend any retriever that ranks documents using a numerical similarity score between a query and a document corpus
The TempRALM retriever uses the standard Atlas-large

why_unaddressed: Retrieval-agnosticism is stated as a design property rather than tested as an empirical claim, and the only instantiation reported is a single dense retriever on a non-legal corpus.
research_question: Is the effect of a temporal re-ranking wrapper stable across sparse and dense retrievers under matched budgets, or specific to one embedding space?
potential_experiment: Apply the identical temporal re-ranking wrapper to BM25 and at least two dense encoders on the same benchmark, with matched passage segmentation, top-k and generator, and report whether the sign and size of the effect are stable across retrievers.
verification_required: Requires the cross-retriever experiment; also a search for retriever-agnostic temporal wrappers in other domains.
